additional_concerns: The permission assessments distinguish an authorized option from sufficient conditions for its use. Reading either format claim merely as identifying an option supports its core; reading its listed conditions as exhaustive does not. NOT_ESTABLISHED does not mean XML or PDF submission is prohibited.

Footnote 3 is available. da12aecad4e68.u30.3569 states exactly: "Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission." Both XML and PDF entries carry marker 3. Their extraction uncertainties should be corrected; availability does not excuse omitting the qualification. The web-form entry has no marker 3, so extending this e-Cert requirement to every submission method is unsupported by the packet.

The four declared dependencies—missing.39ffa0d54487ee68b17a36b8, missing.da4d23ff33f664a99e4bf8cc, missing.f5f807738efdd34996b25ddc and missing.1557ee52aade13863ae98bda—all have null source_hash values and no description or source binding. Their identities and relevance cannot be inferred. Empty dependency_ids in the scoped checks avoid fabricating mappings; they do not assert that all authority is available.

Missing materials include the prescribed PDF form and separately supplied JFIU XML schema. The linked registration form and webinar presentation are also not supplied. da12aecad4e68.u28.3334 states: "The JFIU will provide guidance to facilitate the re-submission." That guidance is absent; its contents cannot be assumed. These absences do not negate duties expressly stated in the retained circular.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses exactly: "Result: all of these conditions hold: [[the fact filing_date] is greater than or equal to [date value 2026-02-02]; it is not the case that [the fact via_streams2]]". This includes filings before 9:00am on 2 February. da12aecad4e68.u3.811 says "With effect from 2 February 2026, STREAMS 2 will become the only channel for filing STRs2." However, da12aecad4e68.u13.2131 says "upon the launch of STREAMS 2 at 9:00am on 2 February 2026", and the resubmission clause uses "following its implementation". Retain the calendar-date and operational-launch interpretations; the date-only expression does not preserve the latter for pre-9:00am events.

The operational-launch candidates adopt an inclusive boundary. For example, node.8c5e0d91275b795d477f7913 states exactly: "at_or_after_operational_launch: The filing occurs at or after the 9:00am operational launch on 2026-02-02. (Boolean temporal classification)". The source supplies the launch time but no explicit governing timezone in the retained text. Its phrase "following its implementation" also requires interpretation at the exact boundary. External classification does not itself establish either interpretation.

The event candidates differ in scope semantics. node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb states "Scope: the fact licensed_firm" and puts submitted_to_jfiu in the result; the other event candidates put actual STR filing in scope. For a licensed actor's non-submission, the first can return FALSE while the others return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Whether such inputs belong to the typed unit "one original submission event" must be resolved before treating these candidates as equivalent.

Channel classification must remain distinct from format compliance. A STREAMS 2 submission that lacks e-Cert or uses a nonconforming XML schema is not thereby established to be a submission through another channel. Conversely, a FALSE resubmission trigger does not grant permission or establish compliant filing. Adding format, e-Cert or registration requirements as trigger conditions would need separate source support.

The blackout provision in da12aecad4e68.u12.1941 says exactly: "(b)  for any STRs requiring urgent submission during the blackout period of STREAMS, please contact the JFIU directly by email (jfiu@police.gov.hk), phone at 2866 3366 or fax at 2529 4013;". Contact alone does not establish a completed submission. Nor does this text establish that every contact cannot include an actual submission. Preserve that factual distinction and do not generalize the post-implementation channel rule into the blackout.

node.fc565a946804e1633024b4d3 states exactly: "Result: the fact report_has_postlaunch_other_channel_submission". The executable expression does not quantify over events or verify history completeness; these tasks are delegated to the supplied aggregate. A known FALSE requires evidence sufficient to exclude qualifying events, not merely the absence of a recorded event. The runtime's UNKNOWN handling does not verify that evidence.

The report-history candidate scopes the report's responsible entity, while node.8caddb7a4c29338c1d340db1 scopes the original submitter. The source addresses licensed firms but does not resolve every case involving agents, transferred responsibility or different submitting entities. Their factual classifications need an explicit attribution rule before equivalence can be established.

The historical trigger questions do not ask whether a duty remains outstanding. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission can concern performance of a duty without erasing the original triggering event. No candidate should be interpreted as an outstanding-duty test without additional logic and authority.

The XML transition provision requires liaison to arrange a technical test; it does not expressly make successful test completion a precondition for permission. Likewise, the registration instruction's SHOULD must not become MUST. These would be additional restrictions unsupported by the retained wording.

The declared convention "Declared output convention: TRUE_IS_SATISFIED" must be interpreted through each typed question: TRUE here means that a duty is triggered, not that it has been satisfied. None of the NOT_APPLICABLE assessments establishes overall candidate correctness or authorizes deleting the retained pairs.
